Nxeon (VPS/game-hosting business, production Next.js app at /opt/nxeon). Phase 3 of NxLabs (the mod/plugin catalog) is starting. This task: build a real Thunderstore-based import pipeline, following the exact conventions of the existing Modrinth pipeline.

## Context you need
- `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts` is the reference pattern: dry-run by default behind `scripts/db-target-guard.ts`, upserts on `GameMod`'s `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])`, idempotent (safe to re-run, must produce `created=0` on a second run). Read it in full before writing anything.
- `prisma/schema.prisma`'s `GameMod` model — check current exact fields before writing, but includes: gameFamily, source, sourceId, slug, name, description, iconUrl, galleryUrls[], authorName, authorAvatarUrl, downloads, license, gameVersions[], loaders[], serverSide, active, featured, popularity.
- Legal policy already established (do not deviate): Thunderstore has confirmed NO license field anywhere in their API or manifest spec, and NO published Terms of Service at all (verified 5 independent ways earlier this session). Default copyright applies — this means FETCH-AT-INSTALL-TIME ONLY, never mirror/rehost the actual mod file into our own storage. Set `license` to null/unconfirmed, never fabricate a license value.
- API is fully open, unauthenticated, real: `https://thunderstore.io/c/{community}/api/v1/package/` — confirmed live, returns real JSON arrays. Confirmed real field shape (verify live, don't assume, but from earlier research): `name`, `full_name`, `owner`, `package_url`, dates, `categories`, `versions[]` (each version has its own download url + real per-version data), `is_deprecated` likely present — check live.
- Games/communities to import, in this priority order:
  1. `valheim` — the deepest, most real Thunderstore coverage (confirmed ~11,459 packages earlier this session). Check first whether any `source:"thunderstore"` GameMod rows already exist for valheim from Phase 1 (a placeholder/small batch may already exist) — if so, treat this as a real bulk expansion/upsert, not a from-scratch import, and don't duplicate.
  2. `sons-of-the-forest` — confirmed live via `https://thunderstore.io/c/sons-of-the-forest/api/v1/package/` earlier this session (uses BepInExPack IL2CPP loader).
  3. `schedule-i` — confirmed real and currently popular game (Steam appid 3164500, ~11K daily players), moddable via MelonLoader, Thunderstore community exists at `https://thunderstore.io/c/schedule-i/`.
  4. `sunkenland` — confirmed real but thin Thunderstore coverage (~45 packages per earlier research) — import what's there.
- Apply a real quality gate similar to Modrinth's (e.g. skip deprecated packages, maybe a minimum download-count threshold for the huge Valheim set specifically so you don't import 11,000+ near-zero-download packages as "featured" content — use judgment, document your threshold and why in the script's comments, the same way Modrinth's `downloads>1000 OR follows>50` gate is documented).
- Real icon: Thunderstore's package icon is typically at a predictable CDN URL pattern per-version — check the live API response for the actual icon field/URL shape rather than guessing, and use the real one.
- Author: Thunderstore's `owner` field is the real uploader — use it as authorName (note: this is often the packager, not necessarily the original mod author for reposted content — if the package data distinguishes this anywhere, prefer the real original author; if not, use owner and don't overclaim).

## Process (mandatory)
- Read `scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts` and `prisma/schema.prisma` in full first.
- Check `lib/mod-install-support.ts`'s `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES` — thunderstore should already be listed as resolvable (Phase 1 built basic Thunderstore support); verify `worker/game-mods.ts`'s `resolveUrl()` already handles thunderstore correctly for the new games you're adding (sons-of-the-forest, schedule-i, sunkenland used different game-family strings than valheim — make sure gameFamily values you write match this repo's actual `GameFamily` type in `lib/games.ts`, and if schedule-i/sons-of-the-forest/sunkenland aren't yet real families Nxeon hosts under those exact keys, check `lib/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_CONTROL` keys from earlier research — sunkenland IS a real existing family key there; sons-of-the-forest is `sonsoftheforest`; schedule-i's game-family key needs to be added if `schedule1` doesn't already exist as one — check first, this repo already has `schedule1` in `GAME_CONTROL` per earlier research this session).
- DB reads/writes only via `db` from `lib/db`, scripts under `scripts/_tmp-*.ts` via `npx tsx`, delete when done. NEVER print/construct a raw psql/DATABASE_URL string — this is a hard rule, a plaintext DB password leaked from a sibling agent's raw `.env` cat just today.
- Dry-run first, verify sane sample output, then `--apply`, then re-run once to confirm idempotency (`created=0` second time).
- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Build via `bash scripts/deploy-staging.sh main` (never build directly in /opt/nxeon), verify staging, then `bash scripts/promote-production.sh`, confirm BUILD_ID changed + fresh service ActiveEnterTimestamp.
- Add a dated entry to `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`.
- Commit, confirm it reached `origin/main`.

Report back: real counts imported per game family, the quality-gate threshold you chose and why, confirmation of idempotency, and confirmation nothing was mirrored/downloaded into our own storage (fetch-at-install only).

import { PrismaClient } from "@prisma/client";

const globalForPrisma = globalThis as unknown as { prisma?: PrismaClient };

export const db = globalForPrisma.prisma ?? new PrismaClient();

if (process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production") globalForPrisma.prisma = db;
---
#!/bin/bash
# Promote the currently deployed staging commit to production.
# Verifies staging is healthy, fast-forwards nothing (prod working tree IS the repo),
# then rebuilds + restarts production services.
set -euo pipefail

STG_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon-staging rev-parse HEAD)
PROD_COMMIT=$(git -C /opt/nxeon rev-parse HEAD)

echo "==> Staging is at:    $STG_COMMIT"
echo "==> Production is at: $PROD_COMMIT"

if ! systemctl is-active -q nxeon-staging-web; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging web service is not running." >&2
  exit 1
fi
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
if [ "$CODE" != "200" ]; then
  echo "Refusing to promote: staging returns HTTP $CODE." >&2
  exit 1
fi

if [ "$STG_COMMIT" != "$PROD_COMMIT" ]; then
  echo "Note: production tree is at a different commit than staging."
  echo "Production deploys directly from /opt/nxeon's working tree (main)."
fi

cd /opt/nxeon
echo "==> Installing dependencies (adds any new deps before build)"
# CRITICAL: without this, a commit that adds a new dependency (e.g. imapflow)
# builds against a stale node_modules and fails — which previously aborted the
# promote AFTER the old build was already gone. Always sync deps first.
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -3
# CRITICAL: this was previously `prisma generate` only — regenerates the
# CLIENT's types (fixes the build) but never touches the actual DATABASE.
# Staging and production are SEPARATE databases (nxeon_staging vs nxeon, same
# Postgres server, confirmed live) — deploy-staging.sh's own `db push` only
# ever applies to staging's DB, so a schema change promoted this way built
# and deployed fine while production's actual table never got the new
# column, silently breaking the FIRST thing that queried it post-deploy
# (found live 2026-09-02: worker/billing.ts's sweeps started throwing
# "column does not exist" immediately after a routine promote — no staging
# failure gave any warning, since staging's own db push had already
# succeeded there). `db push` both applies the schema AND regenerates the
# client, so this replaces the old generate-only step rather than adding a
# second one. Schema changes are rare enough that this always running
# unconditionally costs nothing when there's nothing new to push.
echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss --schema=/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma 2>&1 | tail -4
echo "==> Building production"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4
# Guard: never restart into an incomplete/failed build. A valid production build
# always writes .next/BUILD_ID; if it's missing the build failed mid-way and the
# old in-memory process is still serving — abort rather than kill it.
if [ ! -s /opt/nxeon/.next/BUILD_ID ]; then
  echo "BUILD FAILED: .next/BUILD_ID missing — NOT restarting (old process left serving)." >&2
  exit 1
fi
# next.config sets output:"standalone"; the standalone server.js is what the
# systemd unit actually runs (not `next start` — see deploy-staging.sh's own
---staging---
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker

## NxLabs Phase 3 — real Thunderstore import pipeline, 4 new game catalogues (2026-09-20)

**What landed.** `scripts/import-thunderstore-catalog.ts` — the Thunderstore counterpart to
`scripts/import-modrinth-catalog.ts`, same dry-run-by-default/`db-target-guard`/upsert-on-
`@@unique([gameFamily, slug])`/idempotent shape. Pulls Thunderstore's real, open, unauthenticated v1
catalogue API (`https://thunderstore.io/c/{community}/api/v1/package/` — one request per community
returns its ENTIRE package list, no pagination, confirmed live) for four communities and writes real
`GameMod` rows: **valheim** (gameFamily `valheim`, already had 21 hand-picked Phase 1 rows — this is a
genuine bulk expansion onto them, not a from-scratch import), **sons-of-the-forest** (`sonsoftheforest`),
**schedule-i** (`schedule1`), **sunkenland** (`sunkenland`) — all three family keys confirmed to already
exist in `lib/games.ts`'s `GAME_FAMILIES` / `lib/game-control.ts`'s `GAME_CONTROL` before writing anything.

**Quality gate (all documented in the script's own header, not repeated in full here).** Every
community skips `is_deprecated` packages (real and large: 45.8% of valheim's raw 11,522) and
`has_nsfw_content` packages, and skips anything tagged `Client-side` without also `Server-side` (this
repo's own `GameMod.serverSide` doc comment: a client-only mod "cannot be installed on a server at all,
and the catalogue should not offer it" — only valheim actually uses this tag pair in practice, removing
1,204 client-only packages there). Valheim ALONE additionally requires the latest version's real
download count `> 1,000` — its raw catalogue is 11,522 packages, so without a floor the "genuinely
popular" signal would drown in near-zero-download noise; the other three communities are already small
(81/523/45 raw) so no floor is applied there, matching "import what's there." Considered and rejected a
Modrinth-style second disjoint pass on `rating_score` (Thunderstore's closest thing to Modrinth's
"follows"): checked live how many packages a rating-based pass would catch that the downloads floor
